title: Poisson-primed-burst-emulator-with-dynamic-primer-scheduler-and-attenuation-reporter
author: Anya Patel
description: Context: We need a lightweight, production-faithful way to synthesize bursty traffic that follows a Poisson arrival process but includes priming/skewed context behavior observed in chat workloads. Motivation: existing runners focus on deterministic sequences or heavy tailed bursts; they miss short-lived context-priming effects that drive KV-cache pressure and tail latency spikes. This PR introduces a Poisson-primed burst emulator that supports dynamic primer schedules, per-session attenuation (to model user drop-off), and emits a compact attenuation report for upstream telemetry. What changed: added a new runner (benchlab/runners/poisson_emulator.py) that implements multi-session Poisson arrival with configurable primer sequences and primer reuse policy; added a Go CLI shim (cmd/poisson-emulator/main.go) for cluster runs and KVCheat mode; added a Rust reporter (benchlab/reporters/attenuation_reporter.rs) that consumes runner traces and exports per-cohort attenuation curves + p99 tail deltas; new docs and examples (docs/benchlab/poisson_emulator.md) and a CI workflow (ci/bench-runner.yml) to run the scenario on the canary infra. Key features: - Poisson arrival engine with lambda schedule per-epoch - Dynamic primer scheduler: supports static, rolling, and heatmap-based primer selection - Attenuation model: configurable half-life parameter to emulate context-reuse decay - Session stickiness and reuse window for KV-cache semantics - Output: compact NDJSON trace lines, cohort labels, and aggregated attenuation metrics Why this matters: this runner reproduces short-lived priming that can cause transient p95/p99 regressions even when steady-state throughput looks stable; it helps validate batching, KV-cache checkpointing, and scheduler heuristics. How to run locally: python3 benchlab/runners/poisson_emulator.py --config experiments/poisson/small.yaml || For cluster: ./bin/poisson-emulator --config experiments/poisson/canary.yaml --kve-mode=reuse Tests & validation: unit tests for arrival engine and primer scheduler included; end-to-end run against a small canary cluster produced a baseline report showing a 12% delta in p99 when primer half-life was reduced from 30s to 8s (attached in PR artifacts). Backwards compatibility: runner is opt-in and lives under benchlab/runners; no changes to existing canonical workloads. Linear/Jira: ENG-2314 ENG-2412 Checklist: [x] runner implementation [x] CLI shim [x] reporter and aggregation [x] unit tests [x] docs and example configs [x] CI job Notes: tuned default lambda values for synthetic chat-like pace; added guard rails to avoid generating extremely high QPS by mistake. Related: follows up on prototype in ENG-1886 and uses signal format adopted in ENG-2490. Merge: squash and merge.
